summary.name: Bruno
summary.one_liner: Bruno is a Git-native, open-source API client for REST, GraphQL, gRPC and WebSocket that stores collections as plain-text files on your machine.
use_cases: version control API collections alongside code
testing REST, GraphQL, gRPC or WebSocket endpoints
replacing a cloud-based API platform with a local client
reviewing API request changes through Git pull requests
keeping API data private on a local machine
summary.what_it_does: Bruno stores API collections as folders and plain-text files in a repository, so they can be branched, diffed, reviewed and merged with normal Git workflows. It supports REST, GraphQL, gRPC and WebSocket requests. The page states there is no cloud sync, no account or login required, and that data stays on the user's machine unless shared through Git. It is described as built on OpenCollection, an open standard for API collections, and as running within an organization's existing security setup without a cloud tenant.
notable: Collections stored as plain-text files in the repo, usable with Git
Local-only with no cloud sync, no account, and no login
Built on OpenCollection, an open standard for API collections
Listed on awesome-mac as an offline-only, git-friendly open-source API client
caveats: Platform support is not named on the page beyond general 'your machine' and 'your IDE' references
Sharing happens only through Git, with no built-in cloud sharing
